Understanding the Indrive User Experience

text: Medium Understanding the Indrive User Experience BY: Ogechi Ezekwe Learning ID: ALT/SOP/KAR/026/0042 | by Ogechi Ezekwe | Nov, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Ogechi Ezekwe Product Management Ogechi Ezekwe 2 min read · Nov 2, 2026 -- Listen Share Understanding the Indrive User Experience BY: Ogechi Ezekwe Learning ID: ALT/SOP/KAR/026/0042 Introduction Indrive is a ride-hailing app that connects passengers with drivers who can take them to their destinations. Unlike some other ride-hailing apps, Indrive allows passengers to suggest how much they are willing to pay for a trip and the prices are fixed. Drivers can either accept the offer or suggest another price. Problem statement This gives passengers some control over how much they spend on transportation. However, some challenges a passenger may experience is finding a driver who accepts their offer, especially during busy periods or when travelling to less popular locations, a couple of people complained about the rickety cars based on the survey, and the time it takes for drivers to arrive. Take a look at the survey carried out among users of the Indrive app: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZvzbzujsX8RvUatyrf7TY_pG0-Sxlc6Qc82KMn9kMKg/edit?usp=sharing User Persona Press enter or click to view image in full size User Journey Map Press enter or click to view image in full size The biggest pain point is the condition of some vehicles operating on the platform. Passengers pay for a ride expecting a comfortable and safe journey. However, some vehicles are poorly maintained, dirty or uncomfortable. This can affect passengers trust in the platform, the time the driver arrives due to the condition of the car and the comfort of the customer. Recommendation I would recommend introducing a vehicle quality and inspection feature. This could include: 1. Requiring drivers to upload pictures of their vehicles. 2. Introducing vehicle condition checks before approval. 3. Allowing passengers to report vehicles in poor condition. 4. Reviewing repeated complaints and taking appropriate action against vehicles that fail the required standards . Conclusion Looking at the Indrive experience has helped me understand that getting a ride at an affordable and fixed price is not the only thing passengers care about. The condition of the vehicle also plays a big part in how they feel about the service. A passenger may get a driver quickly and agree on a reasonable fare, but if the car is dirty, uncomfortable or poorly maintained, the overall experience can still be disappointing. As someone interested in product management, this exercise has taught me the importance of looking beyond the features an app offers and paying attention to what happens when people actually use the service. Ultimately, a good ride-hailing experience should not just be about getting passengers to their destinations. It should also be about making sure they feel safe, comfortable and satisfied throughout the journey.
